name: APT1
affiliation_detail:
Mandiant's February 2013 report provided "evidence linking APT1 to China's 2nd Bureau of the People's Liberation Army (PLA) General Staff Department's (GSD) 3rd Department," unit 61398.
In May 2014, the DOJ indicted five Unit 61398 officers — Wang Dong (王东, aka "UglyGorilla"), Sun Kailiang (孙凯亮, aka "Jack Sun"), Wen Xinyu (文新宇, aka "WinXYHappy"), Huang Zhenyu (黄振宇), and Gu Chunhui (顾春晖, aka "KandyGoo") — on 31 criminal counts including economic espionage, theft of trade secrets, and computer fraud. This was the first-ever U.S. indictment of known state actors for cyber espionage. (DOJ, 2014)
description:
APT1 is a Chinese state-sponsored cyber espionage group attributed to PLA Unit 61398, the 2nd Bureau of the PLA General Staff Department's 3rd Department, based in Shanghai's Pudong district. The group is the subject of the first-ever U.S. criminal indictment against state actors for cyber espionage.
Between 2006 and 2013, Mandiant observed APT1 compromise at least 141 organizations across 20 major industries, "systematically stolen hundreds of terabytes of data," with the capability "to steal from dozens of organizations simultaneously." The group maintained persistent access for an average of 356 days per victim, with the longest single intrusion lasting 1,764 days (four years and ten months). The largest observed single theft was 6.5 terabytes of compressed data from one organization over ten months. Of the 141 known victims, 87% were headquartered in English-speaking countries, with 115 in the United States. Targeted industries aligned with China's 12th Five-Year Plan strategic priorities. (Mandiant, 2013)
The aliases including "comment" were derived from the group's utilization of C2 instructions embedded in HTML comment tags on legitimate-looking web pages.  Later, APT1 also utilized other tags. (Mandiant, 2013)
APT1 infrastructure was largely dismantled following the February 2013 Mandiant report.

campaigns.name: Economic espionage against U.S. corporations (DOJ Indictment)
campaigns.description: Five PLA Unit 61398 officers (Wang Dong, Sun Kailiang, Wen Xinyu, Huang Zhenyu, Gu Chunhui) conducted sustained cyber intrusions against six U.S. entities—Westinghouse Electric, SolarWorld AG (U.S. subsidiaries), U.S. Steel, Allegheny Technologies Inc., the United Steelworkers Union, and Alcoa— stealing trade secrets, proprietary manufacturing data, business strategy documents, and privileged attorney-client communications in the nuclear power, metals, and solar products industries.
